# Index

LTE modem ~$3-6/mo, eSIM-vs-physical-SIM; device architecture on flexpay); **Jun-23** Val's reach-out to Texas operators Jordan & Joe (introduced via Steven at AMOT → Austin): pitch gaming-now + the September transactional set, Class-III/skill certification (GLI-11/12, GLI + Eclipse labs, Nebraska skill), and ship one machine to Austin for Steve to vet; JVL skips G2E but will be at AMOE/AMOA (69 sources, updated 2026-10-17)

## Decisions

### Corporate & Finance
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-05-erase-replace-labs-gl-reduce-chart-of-accounts.md]] — (Aug-5 2026, active) erase & replace JVL Labs GL (no entries to preserve) and reduce the chart to 146 posting accounts for Systems / 96 for Labs (from ~800); process rule: a change is accepted only if all three of Cris/Igor/Laura back it, remarks in column J; leaning (not locked) to freeze JVL Systems history and start clean, deferring to the AI CFO / Sean Riley (2 sources, updated 2026-08-06)

- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-06-open-cibc-us-accounts-starting-with-jvl-systems.md]] — open CIBC US accounts one at a time, starting with JVL Systems Inc. (1 source, updated 2026-07-12)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-03-24-close-jvl-mexico-operation.md]] — wind down/dissolve JVL Mexico (announce after the 3rd shipment; Erica + technician let go; Colombia kept); tightened Apr-7 to **30 days / ~$20k budget, close ~May 15** (Miguel+Camilo retrieve ~100 machines; severance discretionary, "null and void" letter if not closed by May); Jul-3 the 2019 tax-audit status (two of three findings settled in June conciliation, ISR ~$77k→~$11k; depreciation open, ~6M-peso assessment expected ~6mo; multi-component defence; Val's 2020–2025 book-restatement idea; JVL Mexico owned by JVL Mobi Canada shell) (7 sources, updated 2026-07-19)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-05-29-eds-fx-conversion-cost-routing.md]] — split the missed US↔COP bank FX-conversion charge on EDS payments 50/50 (mutual omission), but re-route payments (JVL→Eliana's Miami account; EDS→Elevate directly) to avoid it; Elevate non-approval judged unlikely to actually block payment (1 source, updated 2026-07-17)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-06-17-implement-then-replace-business-central.md]] — finish/run the Business Central rollout (kept simple, no manufacturing module) for the learning curve, then move JVL off it to a simple/cheaper system; rationale = BC is "shooting birds with a cannon" + SaaS UIs will be replaced by AI within ~3 years (1 source, updated 2026-07-17)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-06-24-move-manufacturing-from-canada-to-georgia.md]] — stop manufacturing in Canada, move assembly to a new 10,500 sq ft Louisville (Atlanta) warehouse (tariff risk; nothing ties JVL to Canada; keep JVL Canada alive for tax losses); Elizabeth heads manufacturing, Anibal assembles Echo, logistics stays with Mary; DDP quotes + a US metal fabricator; BC assembly with no manufacturing module; History adds the Jul-2024 "Canadian Manufacturing Operations Closure Plan" antecedent (same move planned for Dec-31-2024 but not fully executed; 100 Flex sets/40 Echo/500 parts, 5,000 sq ft aux warehouse; date-conflict QUEUED — doc internally dates 2024, staged as 2025) (0 sources, updated 2026-07-20)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-07-15-exit-online-focus-transactional.md]] — Val stops actively pursuing the online-gaming/RGS business (can't compete; $1M online needs far more capital) and pours effort into transactional products + ECHO amusement; finish in-flight integrations, take no new ones, release the online contractors; parked-not-dead (active) (2 sources, updated 2026-07-20)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-07-jvl-labs-ccpc-trust-held-pending-the-gaar-ruling.md]] — (Sept-7 2026, active) the Canadian-resident trust that would keep **JVL Labs a CCPC** — holding the Labs shares — is **NOT put in place** until the GAAR position is clear after the mid-October Tax Court hearing, because the adviser will not expose Val to a 50% penalty in the meantime. What is at stake is the SR&ED credit: lose CCPC status and the provincial portion goes entirely, the federal portion only offsets profits JVL does not have. The trigger is control of JVL Labs passing outside Canada. The case name is transcribed "Polisat" and is **not asserted to be a real case name**; aka CCPC trust held, GAAR hold (2 sources, updated 2026-09-07)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-15-mutual-nda-agreed-clause-12-deleted-and-clause-8-time-boxed.md]] — the mutual NDA between JVL and Billy Liu's PlayPay settled live on the call: **Clause 12 (non-compete) deleted outright** — "I'm not here to tie you down… get rid of the clause" — **Clause 8 time-boxed**, the three-year term kept, and the **effective date corrected from 2024 to Sept 15 2026** by Val in the document while they spoke; both sides' signing commitments remain **open** because no signature is recorded anywhere, even though Billy later says "We signed an NDA. We're going to keep it"; open — what the NDA's "normal period" means and which entity actually signed; status active (3 sources, updated 2026-09-19)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-07-08-jvl-labs-charges-jvl-systems-software-licensing-fees-sourced-to-florida.md]] — From 2026 JVL Labs charges JVL Systems software-licensing (maybe head-office) fees, benefit sourced to Florida — replaces the machine-sales route; arm's-length price; transfer-pricing study agreed (Jul-8 2026) (1 source, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-29-val-writes-the-capital-call-letter-asking-one-to-two-million-and-litwack-writes-the-dilution-part.md]] — Sept 29: a written letter to all partners asks $1–2M, moderately optimistic after the trade show; Val writes his part, Litwack writes the dilution part ("no equity in JVL after that debt"); Val expects the partners will not contribute; aka capital call letter to the partners, dilution part of the letter (2 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-29-the-investor-write-off-structure-is-checked-so-nobody-can-say-jvl-helped-disguise-anything.md]] — Sept 29: Litwack accepts the $4,000-now / $15,000-write-off model as deferred payment but requires it be checked by his US people so "nobody in the IRS can say you helped them disguise something"; Val agrees; aka structure it better, US people review of the write-off (3 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-08-mary-takes-over-mikhail-perelmans-ordering-role-with-training-from-october-19.md]] — Mikhail Perelman leaves from January; Mary (Mery) takes over ordering — decided for now (owner 2026-10-15), training from Oct 19 through November and half of December (Oct 8 2026); aka Misha leaves, Mery takes over, procurement hand-over (13 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-13-new-incomm-terms-go-onto-the-existing-written-agreement.md]] — new InComm terms (Val's guarantee and half-percent items) go onto the existing written agreement; its $300,000 wire cap is to be thought through (Oct 13 2026); aka go back to what's on paper (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-13-business-central-is-the-only-source-of-truth-for-vendor-bank-details-and-wires-take-them-from-it-every-time.md]] — wires take vendor bank details from Business Central every time — no templates kept at the bank, no manual entry; the advanced CashPro platform if the base one cannot (Oct 13 2026); aka laborious and unacceptable (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-13-customers-start-their-own-recurring-ach-payments-through-a-portal-against-a-signed-agreement.md]] — customers set up their own recurring ACH through a portal against a signed agreement; every payment method offered, each fee told in advance and paid by the customer (Oct 13 2026); aka customer ACH portal (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-16-val-and-lev-focus-together-on-inventory-control-so-mary-can-run-ordering-alone.md]] — Val and Lev fix inventory control (receipts, production postings, invoicing) together so Mary can run it alone and Lev moves to standards/automation; aka fix inventory control, вдвоём сфокусируемся (4 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-19-mary-asks-business-central-through-mcp-not-special-reports-and-nathan-adds-msbc-endpoints-from-ai-coo-use-cases.md]] — Val (Oct 19): no special reports for Mary — she asks Business Central through MCP in Spanish or English; Nathan adds MSBC endpoints for end-to-end inventory control from the AI COO use cases; purchase-invoice gaps noted; aka AI COO use cases, MSBC endpoints (4 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-20-the-procurement-admin-system-comes-first-and-cost-cuts-new-suppliers-and-machine-redesign-wait-for-january.md]] — Val (Oct 20): with 45 working days left, the admin procurement system comes first; cost cuts, new suppliers, amplifier and machine redesign wait for January; harnesses ordered, not hand-made; TVs at $46 test order; Val and Genadi talk daily; aka 45 working days (4 sources, updated 2026-10-24)

### Hardware & Cabinets

- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-07-order-limited-retrofit-parts.md]] — order only 50 monitors + ~200 CPU kits + Altera buttons now; wait to assess Maple (1 source, updated 2026-07-12)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-08-ship-100-best-machines-from-mexico.md]] — ship the 100 best machines first, two trucks by ground to Georgia (1 source, updated 2026-07-12)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-08-scrap-and-write-off-unusable-machines.md]] — scrap unrestorable machines with an external-auditor count for write-off (1 source, updated 2026-07-12)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-13-adopt-fp7-for-flex-s-fortune-fu-paws.md]] — adopt the FP7 board for Flex-S / Fortune Fu Paws on the Omni platform (1 source, updated 2026-07-12)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-17-remain-on-fp7-hardware-ceiling.md]] — after bottleneck testing, stay on FP7 and optimize rather than upgrade; CPU is the limit (1 source, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-22-support-epic-950-printer-for-south-dakota.md]] — support the Transact Epic 950 printer for South Dakota; enable CRC validation, add volume-to-zero, ship unapproved software for lab testing (1 source, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-02-27-flex-street-cabinet-design-direction.md]] — Flex V42/C street cabinet: remove chrome, one carbon-fiber upper surface, hidden speakers, floating curved monitor, keep tracking-bracket dims; credit-card reader now a requirement; **Jun-8-2026** a new cost-driven low-cost "street" machine direction (target whole device under $2,000 incl. bill acceptor; strip cabinet to one door + single 43" monitor; Rockchip board dropping amplifier/light/counters/VDEC ~$500-600; self-built bill-path "nose"/bezel with integrated QR reader replacing the $35 plastic nose + player-tracking port) (4 sources, updated 2026-07-30)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-21-back-to-back-two-player-cabinet-direction.md]] — (Aug-21 2026, active) cabinet direction: **back-to-back two-player slant-top** (single monitor + VDEC per player, triangular/45° topper, FP7 drives 4 monitors, Georgia gas stations); **multi-play (one player / 4 games, Wonder 4) killed** (tiny symbols, discouraging math) but NOVA keeps the graphics/CPU/memory headroom; shared-single-screen concepts dropped; the one-machine/one-serial prize is blocked by SAS (open Q); complements the platform's simultaneous-multi-game support on nova-platform-architecture (2 sources, updated 2026-08-21)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-03-21-hg6-support-legacy-and-new-button-panels.md]] — HG6 software supports both legacy and new button panels via one XML key-code mapping, so one build serves retrofit + kit machines with no manual selection (2 sources, updated 2026-07-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-03-27-preliminary-industrial-design-all-three-flex-cabinets.md]] — design all three Flex machines (curve/243/"Dnavi") as one family before detailing; amplifier box on the base unit; monitor-angle + light-fixture changes; via Igor Starovoytov (1 source, updated 2026-07-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-03-27-invest-in-flex-sound-and-power-redesign.md]] — approve a Flex sound + power redesign (new power distributor/regulators/converters, uprated amplifier, high-fidelity speakers) at a ~$200 component budget (1 source, updated 2026-07-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-04-16-dispensing-tower-first-magnetic-stripe.md]] — build the self-serve card-dispensing tower first (before POS), on the FlexPort base (Alekseev/Yavorski), magnetic-stripe-only reader, and rent it (recurring-revenue clearing house, ~$1/transaction); legacy non-FlexPort machines (~3k of 35k) deprioritized (1 source, updated 2026-07-15)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-04-24-standalone-server-in-a-box.md]] — build a standalone Linux "server in a box" (fanless industrial board ~$120–130, Cisco-look enclosure) running JVL accounting host + Incom API + TITO server; Ethernet-only, separate from FlexPay (slave mode); 4 to Toronto / 2 to Minsk (1 source, updated 2026-07-16)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-05-26-arm-linux-platform-flex-devices.md]] — adopt a cheap ARM-based embedded-Linux board (Rockchip RK, ~$60, 2GB/16GB onboard) for Flex Tower / Flex POS / TITO server; resolves the May-20/21 STM-vs-industrial-Linux deferral (Linux flexibility at ~STM price); LVDS adapter + driver via Alekseev, no extra I/O boards; ruled pending sample validation; **reconfirmed June-4** on a formal STM-vs-Linux pros/cons (Linux wins on dev resources + existing Java Passport/Lease/RIS modules; financial-system redundancy/hot-swap framing; ~Oct on-site test); **Nov-5 2025: Rockchip is the production board — update JVL software only (eMMC partition + boot-time USB script, Alekseev), demand full manufacturer deliverables, own-STM-board deferred (~3-month)**; **Nov-11: update model settled (SD-card full image + boot-time script updating only the JVL app on a writable eMMC partition, Linux read-only, backup/rollback); remote update mandatory (FlexPay has none today, only FlexPort in progress); Rockchip stays, STM/NXP/TI ~2× cost dropped, RK3576/RK3588 noted; build-once → supplier-agnostic; Dima Pikulev ruled out again**; **May-29-2026 update: the transactional device category (recycler/dispenser/paystation) also consolidates onto Rockchip off the interim V-1000** (10 sources, updated 2026-07-30)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-24-flex-port-mini-via-second-sas-only.md]] — build Flex-Port-Mini connecting only through the machine's 2nd SAS port (drops the bill-acceptor in-line wiring, the most problematic part); ~$45 build budget for the Mini and ~$250 for the full Flex-Port; a minimal ~$1–5 non-touch info display for the cash-out prompt; stage-1 networking = wired CAT5/RS-485 reusing existing wiring; WiFi, per-port LTE and NFC rejected, Bluetooth mesh un-estimable; machines without a 2nd SAS (~15–20% / ~10–15K units) out of scope; no partial load or partial cash-out; aka second SAS port only, $45 port budget (3 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-24-drop-pin-from-evoucher-flow.md]] — drop the PIN code from the eVoucher flow; a QR voucher is trusted the way a TITO ticket is ("the first ticket is always the original, the second one is not"); Pavel flagged the security trade-off (a copied barcode used before the real player arrives) and got the QR-carries-a-server-URL registration plus per-location playable-only promo credits in exchange; aka eVoucher without PIN, TITO trust model (5 sources, updated 2026-09-19)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-tito-printer-cases-come-before-the-street-cabinet.md]] — Genadi Peari's standalone-peripherals proposal is **rejected** and the **TITO printer enclosure is put ahead of the street cabinet**, with the spec settled in the room: external desktop PSU, RS-232 brought out from the outside, connectors on the back panel, provisioned for **400 tickets** ("сзади чуть побольше… всегда поставить 400") and **no security features**; **plastic, not metal** — 3D-print first, then tooling; the street cabinet itself starts **Sept 23** ("23 можете приступить к кабинету?" — "Думаю да"); status active (3 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-street-cabinet-main-screen-runs-on-lvds-not-a-controller.md]] — the street cabinet's **main screen runs on LVDS with JVL's own cable and adapter**, not a bought controller board (controller $35 against $15–20 for JVL's own, "экономия раунд 15 $20"), with HDMI-plus-controller kept only for the optional second screen; **only Full HD is locked in** ("Только фулл эйч ди мы зашиваем"), against a **$1,000 build target** and the 43″/4K/49″ constraint; **§11 evolution, not contradiction** — this displaces the Jul-29 "LVDS is impractical" position, which is preserved rather than deleted; open — can LVDS actually drive the main screen; status active (5 sources, updated 2026-09-19)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-the-street-cabinet-board-is-the-rk3576-not-the-rk3568.md]] — the street cabinet moves to the **RK3576 with 8 GB** because the **RK3568 renders badly on a vertical screen** ("Но это именно 35 68", per Pavel from the Chinese documentation) — "чуть дороже там $15 из 8 гигабайтами и это как раз таргет"; supply pushed through **Mikhail Perelman** to Minsk (2 samples at $150 plus ~$65 freight, supplier rendered "Touch Intelligent"), SDK and integration repo still outstanding; **§11 evolution** displacing the earlier RK3588/16 GB target, with the unreconciled Jul-29 memory arithmetic flagged as an observation rather than resolved; open — where the RK3576 order stands, and whether 8 GB carries the intended game count; status active (11 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-remote-firmware-update-is-in-mvp1-and-flex-iq-updates-itself-first.md]] — (Sept-14 2026, active) remote firmware update is in MVP 1 — Flex IQ and FlexPay update themselves first; distributing firmware to the Flex-Ports left MVP 1 on Sept-17 and **came BACK into MVP 1 on Sept-28** (capability 146) when the date moved to October 15, and **left again on Oct-15** (MVP 1 keeps only the Flex-Port update by USB stick; remote Flex-Port update is MVP 2); rollback to a previous build stays out (Sept-18) (35 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-16-the-street-machine-carries-two-boards-and-a-new-io-board.md]] — the street machine gets **two boards, not one** — an I/O board and a button/counter board — and the existing all-in-one board is scrapped for a clean sheet ("чистый лист"); the new I/O board carries a USB hub, **2 SAS**, a printer port, a bill-acceptor port supporting **ID003 and ccTalk** (pulse ruled out of gaming outright — "Не годится, не делаем, даже не спрашиваем"), lighting support, front-mounted connections and **4 serial channels**; the amplifier is dropped in favour of the TV's own, no subwoofers, no electromechanical counters, and cell modem plus WiFi are mandatory; the cost tension is recorded honestly — a $60–70 I/O board cannot sit inside a $1,000 machine, and Genadi's "$600 a board" was **self-corrected in the next breath to last year's price** ("Сейчас наверно уже я даже не знаю сколько"), which the derived notes flattened into a present-tense figure; status active (3 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-16-one-fram-chip-instead-of-six-and-low-power-mode-laid-in-but-not-populated.md]] — **six 256 FRAM chips collapse to one**, with per-game statistics (last 10 games and last 50 free spins across 6 games) moved to SD card or eMMC on the explicit acceptance that they "may not always be written correctly", while the ~1 MB of live game state stays in FRAM; **Val reverses himself on low-power mode** and accepts Genadi's lay-in-but-do-not-populate compromise ("если можно компоненты заложить, но not poppelate это окей"); the light controller goes; status active (3 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-16-street-machine-electronics-move-to-eye-level-and-the-monitor-opens-like-a-cupboard-door.md]] — **SUPERSEDED Sept-25 2026 — "the TV simply hangs"; the cabinet goes deeper with a fixed dashboard (see the Sept-25 street-cabinet decision)** — the electronics move **to eye level** in a metal box screwed behind the TV and the monitor is **hinged like a kitchen cupboard door** (≤90°), with no podium, no base and no two-screen conversion; **the decision is driven by field evidence, not preference** — Val holds a recording of technicians refusing to buy JVL machines ("women who can't lift it", "won't work with a board that needs a flashlight") and Genadi concedes on it; board mounting and the main-monitor connector are left **unresolved** because LVDS "умрёт после 10 открытия"; status active (5 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-16-machine-identity-moves-off-the-cabinet-passport-onto-jvls-own-io-board.md]] — the cabinet-bound encrypted passport component is removed and machine identity binds instead to **JVL's own I/O board**, on the reasoning that JVL does not change its own board even when it changes processor suppliers; **this does NOT overturn the Sept-11 "passport is preserved" ruling** — the contents survive on the board's own memory, so that decision stays `active` and was cross-referenced rather than re-statused; the board-change procedure was asked about and left unanswered; status active (2 sources, updated 2026-09-20)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-16-street-machines-skip-gli-so-no-boxes-and-no-tampers-but-nebraska-reopens-it.md]] — Val answers "Нет" to GLI for the street machine, so no enclosure boxes and no tampers, only door monitoring, setup and audit — **then reopens it himself four minutes later over Nebraska** ("сейчас я как-то гребу обратно"); recorded as the unsettled thing it is rather than smoothed into a ruling, with Genadi's recollection of the lab's requirements noted as **self-contradictory inside a minute**; status active (2 sources, updated 2026-09-20)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-15-every-device-carries-its-own-lte-modem-and-sim.md]] — **every device at a location carries its own LTE modem and SIM** — each Flex IQ, each machine, the kiosk — and the location router is explicitly **not** the shared modem ("все 4 или 5 девайсов в себе имеют L[T]E modem живут самодостаточно"); Val asked whether spare modems could fail over to cover a Wi-Fi outage, left open as possibly-not-feasible; **the cost rationale is recorded as UNCLEAR, not as stated** — the derived notes gloss it "because SIM cards and data are cheap" while the transcript says the opposite-leaning "не очень маленькие деньги", and the ruling does not depend on it; status active (4 sources, updated 2026-10-17)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-23-jvl-stops-building-its-own-tito-desktop-box-and-uses-jcm-or-transact-for-now.md]] — Val (Sept-23 2026): JVL stops building its own TITO desktop box "for now" — a bought JCM or TransAct unit connects to the Flex IQ, two options offered to the customer (5 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-23-the-bom-source-of-truth-is-the-latest-design-in-github-and-sync-runs-one-way.md]] — Val (Sept-23 2026): the BOM source of truth is the latest design in GitHub and the GitHub→MSBC sync runs one way only — CONTESTED by Genadi on the BOM half (25 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-24-engineering-plans-to-switch-off-the-passport-check-for-georgia-builds.md]] — Sept-24 2026 (engineers, Val absent): plan to switch off the Passport check for Georgia builds + a server "do not filter" flag — OPEN CONTRADICTION with Val's defence of the Passport the same morning (4 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-24-ris-keeps-the-jvl-serial-number-but-it-becomes-less-binding.md]] — Val (Sept-24 2026): RIS stays linked to the JVL serial "for the record" but less binding; mismatched hardware "restricted, do not allow"; naming options open (1 source, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-24-multiple-qr-scans-go-and-one-final-activation-scan-stays.md]] — Sept-24 2026: the chain of up to six lease/QR scans goes; one final activation scan stays, for machines without a modem only (2 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-24-reducing-factory-resets-is-the-one-urgent-fix.md]] — Val (Sept-24 2026): the one urgent fix is fewer factory resets on ~2,500 field machines; next meeting Sept-25 7 AM (2 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-25-the-ris-rework-mvp1-is-for-flex-machines-only.md]] — Val (Sept-25 2026): the RIS rework MVP 1 covers Flex machines only ("Altera is done"); packaging (~20 approvals vs 2, or an 18-game bundle) still open (3 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-25-felipe-acts-as-product-owner-for-the-ris-rework.md]] — Val (Sept-25 2026): Felipe acts as product owner for the RIS rework — grooms the meeting into use cases, capabilities and requirements, hands to Pavel (features → GitHub branches) and Sebastian (field); review Mon Sept 28 10 AM (4 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-25-the-street-cabinet-goes-deeper-so-the-printer-and-a-tito-front-load-acceptor-sit-on-a-fixed-dashboard.md]] — Val (Sept-25 2026): the street cabinet goes deeper — TITO front-load acceptor only (back-load out), printer left / acceptor right on a fixed dashboard, slide-down play panel + 90° fold-down door holding the electronics; supersedes the Sept-16 cupboard-door design — stands in full (owner ruling 2026-10-05: the Oct-1 panel layout is a proposal under consideration, no decision) (5 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-28-sebastian-takes-the-ris-mvp1-capabilities-into-jira-and-felipe-steps-back.md]] — Val (Sept-28 2026): Sebastian manages the RIS MVP 1 capabilities and linked requirements in Jira under Pavel; Felipe helps in the background; Pavel does features and scheduling, Irina acceptance criteria; no autotests on this work (3 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-28-showing-the-real-cause-of-a-critical-error-moves-to-mvp2.md]] — Val (Sept-28 2026): RIS capability 8 — showing the real cause of a critical error — moves to MVP 2 (3 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-02-pilot-manual-ball-recycling-without-acceptor-and-pick-up-system.md]] — try recycling the balls by hand, with no acceptor and no pick-up system, and let the site give live feedback on players (Oct 2 2026; speakers unnamed); aka manual ball-recycling pilot, the changer will save you money (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-15-payment-terminals-get-a-swappable-backup-battery-and-report-power-loss-so-service-can-be-called.md]] — every payment terminal gets a swappable backup battery with a BMS the processor reads, so it can report power loss and service can be called; Val's retry-then-alert rule for dropped links; aka power-loss alert, BMS (2 sources, updated 2026-10-17)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-19-hardware-repositories-start-with-harness-display-and-sheet-metal-and-the-agent-generates-data-contracts-from-vetted-data-sheets.md]] — Val (Oct 19): hardware parts start from Nathan's folder list (harness, display, sheet metal first) with free content + readme, prose and data contracts (the "one repo per project, three repos first" element reversed Oct 21 — one repository with subfolders); the agent generates data contracts from data sheets Genadi has vetted; aka first three hardware repos (8 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-20-flex-port-mvp1-needs-only-an-easy-release-build-and-the-usb-update-and-alekseev-writes-stm32-freertos-rules-for-claude-review.md]] — Val (Oct 20): Flex-Port MVP 1 needs only an easy release build and the USB update, then 10 locations; no dependence on one developer; Alekseev writes STM32/FreeRTOS rules for Claude review; no schedule until tasks are estimated; aka easy release build, beeper in its own thread (4 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-20-first-light-and-wonder-flex-port-installs-get-a-hand-cut-fit-while-a-proper-fix-is-found.md]] — Oct 20: on Light & Wonder machines the Flex-Port is 1 mm too tall without its back cover (~2 months away); first installs cut by hand; Genadi finds a proper fix and teaches Sebastian to make brackets; aka Light and Wonder 1 mm (2 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-21-hardware-parts-go-into-one-repository-with-subfolders-and-the-first-spike-builds-the-power-supply-bom-automatically.md]] — Val (Oct 21): hardware parts go into one repository with subfolders (reverses Oct-5 "no monorepo" and Oct-19 three repos); first spike builds the power-supply BOM from data contracts and Actions, which Nathan loads into Business Central; Genadi does not build the BOM by hand; aka power supply BOM spike (2 sources, updated 2026-10-24)

### Build-pipeline, GitHub & AI-tooling
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-04-bug-only-against-closed-feature.md]] — (Aug-4 2026, active) a bug only exists against a closed/released feature (problems in dev = scope changes); never reopen a closed capability ("breaks the history"); released-product flow: Customer Support ticket → triage reclassifies (Incident) at capability level → fix features/branch merge to main → ticket closes; Pavel's clone-the-capability idea considered & rejected; ~75% of bugs trace to bad acceptance criteria/tests; **Aug-11 follow-through = the Capability Amendment standard** ([[wiki/decisions/2026-08-11-capability-amendment-post-release-bug.md]]) (3 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-11-capability-amendment-post-release-bug.md]] — (Aug-11 2026, active) the **"Capability Amendment"** standard (v1.0) for post-release bugs — a new dedicated, visually-distinct JIRA issue type whose version field holds the fix version; bugs hang under it (typed Bug/red icon) and drive a fix-branch → PR → merge-to-main → release → close cycle; creating one forces reopening the Requirements to add acceptance criteria + tests (Claude to help find the best-fit requirement); ticket roles Creator(fixed)/Reporter(reassignable)/Assignee; branch-vs-tag release management for old certified builds ruled a *separate* future standard; follows the Aug-4 closed-feature decision (2 sources, updated 2026-08-14)

- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-15-move-to-git-native-build-system.md]] — move JVL's build system off Jenkins to a Git-native, serverless pipeline (5 sources, updated 2026-07-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-15-adopt-github-over-bitbucket.md]] — standardise on GitHub over Bitbucket and migrate repos (1 source, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-15-reduce-build-variants-with-post-build-instrumentation.md]] — collapse build parameters to ~four archetypes; instrumentation post-build (3 sources, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-15-defer-test-tool-purchases.md]] — buy no test-automation tool this year (1 source, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-17-upgrade-omni-to-pixi-8-6.md]] — upgrade the Omni engine to Pixi 8.6 and adopt yearly engine updates (1 source, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-20-github-orgs-mirror-value-streams.md]] — GitHub organizations mirror the Jira value streams; teams own their repos; per-org champions; org-level question reopened Mar 31 (open) (2 sources, updated 2026-07-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-01-21-build-git-native-hello-world-environment-first.md]] — build the three-layer Git-native pipeline to a "Hello World" first (MVP step 1); keep CD separate from the QA test tool (1 source, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-02-11-github-org-naming-and-structure.md]] — GitHub org names = human-readable, capitalised, JVL-prefixed; repos = short lowercase-hyphen, no prefix; 7 orgs mirror the value streams (+ Game Concepts/Designs added Feb 26); + Feb-10 part-1 history; **Sept 9–16 2025 arc: naming convention elaborated into a kebab category/subcategory/component/variant taxonomy + validation tool, and the multi-org list SUPERSEDED — consolidating ~11 orgs → ~2, entering execution** (8 sources, updated 2026-07-21)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-02-11-git-migration-sequence.md]] — migrate repos in stages: Omni/Miranda/FlexPay first, then RGS, then inventory-map all remaining Bitbucket/SVN repos; graphics-dept LFS onboarding Feb 18-26 (4 sources, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-02-12-github-repos-private-by-default.md]] — GitHub repos created private by default; access granted per repository (least-privilege; no write for ~first 3 months) (1 source, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-02-21-separate-game-and-design-repos.md]] — split each game into a "game" repo and a "design" repo (LFS comp art via submodule; build doesn't need the comp art) (2 sources, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-02-26-designer-branching-workflow.md]] — designers use feature/story branches, PR-only merges to main, a branch-lifespan metric (3d amazing→10d worst); applies to PSD files too (1 source, updated 2026-07-13)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-03-12-fork-game-repos-from-generic-template.md]] — new game repos fork (not clone) from a generic template Andrei builds; Val overrode the disabled fork-from-template setting (1 source, updated 2026-07-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-03-17-migrate-rgs-codebase-svn-to-git.md]] — move Efim's codebase off SVN to Git first, then continue Hollywood Bets; staged Jenkins→GitHub-Actions migration; Andrei Bosik does the bulk; Mar-31 progress: RGS cloned, MathEngine repos + submodules plan, Windows-first build; Apr-8 done: math in External as submodules, LFS, local+Jenkins builds (3 sources, updated 2026-07-15)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-03-21-fund-aaron-clayton-bespoke-ai-tools.md]] — Val guarantees paid hours for Aaron (+ Clayton) to build bespoke AI tools he keeps and they may commercialise; first tool = the transcription tool; a "Foray" GitHub space (2 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-03-23-migrate-legacy-cms-svn-to-github-by-features.md]] — move the legacy CMS from SVN to GitHub, organized by feature branches tied to requirements; one repo (modular, not microservices); freeze at ~80%; + the ~Mar-25 review-workflow follow-up; aka CMS migration, Protohost; Apr 14–15 evolution: initial move re-scoped to as-is transfer (see the staged-plan decision) (4 sources, updated 2026-07-15)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-04-15-cms-staged-migration-plan.md]] — CMS moves in stages: don't split the monolith now (~15 SVN repos, shared DB); as-is GitHub move only under Val's five-day rule; CMS 1.5 = same stack + updated libraries, segmented; CMS 2.0 = new-tech initiative in Jira; manifests product prioritized for June Omni; aka CMS 1.5, five-day rule (2 sources, updated 2026-07-15)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-04-16-replace-testers-with-test-engineers.md]] — JVL will have no manual testers; hire/retrain Test Engineers who write automated tests; Anton trains the QA engineers (not writing tests himself — changed decision); Irina has ~5 candidates ready; Apr-17 restated w/ hiring trigger (post the ad now, retrain-or-leave, automate routine manual work via Bosik) (3 sources, updated 2026-07-16)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-04-16-adopt-azure-microsoft-secret-server.md]] — **[superseded 2025-05-28]** secrets-management platform evaluation: the Azure-secret-server *platform* pick is superseded by the Delinea trial (Azure = "not a secret server"); the "manage secrets as assets" control model + assets foundation survive (4 sources, updated 2026-07-17)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-05-28-trial-delinea-secrets-management.md]] — **secrets-manager: KEEPER selected (status: superseded — Delinea trial superseded).** Delinea scored winner over CyberArk on May-28 (Azure = "not a secret server"), but the trial surfaced restrictions → Jul-23 pivot to Keeper (≈$5-7k unlimited-server vs Delinea ≈$22k/per-server, Docker gateway, Entra SSO) → **Aug-15 Val authorized buying/installing Keeper** (mandatory adoption, manual no-import migration). **Owner-confirmed 2026-07-20: Keeper is the choice; retitled + flipped per §3, Aug-15 = superseding evidence.** Core (policy-scored secret server) stands. (3 sources)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-05-12-upgrade-activemq-split-from-white-area-host.md]] — upgrade ActiveMQ + split it out of the White Area Host (CASWH) machine-messaging app to close a RAM-only botnet vulnerability; Docker/3-hour-restart fallback; Jira release VAHV 0.23; "Sergei Sandriev" engineer queued (1 source, updated 2026-07-17)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-03-24-freeze-core-capabilities-before-game-production.md]] — game production only uses frozen, tested core capabilities; no engine/framework change requests mid-production (new capabilities land in core advancement for later games); aka golden rule of game production (2 sources, updated 2026-07-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-04-03-jira-capability-level-and-github-mapping.md]] — insert a "capability" level in Jira (bundle of features) as the executive-demonstrable unit mapped to GitHub feature branches; feature branches ≤1 week, ~3–4-week sprints, "no test no pull", repository=product, SVN→GitHub locked; from the Apr 1–3 Val/Aaron arc; flatten-vs-many-orgs still open; + the Apr-3 Aaron session's gears/clutch analogy + Juan/Pavel/Sasha role split; May-5–6 refinement (feature=temporary vs capability=permanent, component, double-diamond, Jira Product Discovery/PLM, capability-replaces-product-line direction — no new ruling); May-8 Compass as engineer-side "second diamond" + Val's core-tech capability maturation (coin→bill→ticket example, RIS as capability) — Compass adoption agreement-in-principle, not enacted; May-9 the value-stream→product→capability→feature→story→subtask tree + rename-Feature→Capability direction; May-12 the double-diamond discovery→capability→feature chain (no ruling); Aug-22 "Specification-Driven Development Process v2.0" written artifact (Val/Pavel/Irina Shishko: "no code without specification", JIRA CAP-XXX → Create-Branch → /specifications/CAP-XXX.md → code+tests; roles Juan=business-PM, Nathan/Will=technical-PM bridge, Pavel=eng-director, Sasha Biratka=dev, Irina+Evgeny Kharetski=QA; phased 5-spec→30%→80% coverage rollout); Sept-2025 the flatten-vs-many-orgs open question RESOLVED (consolidate ~11 orgs → ~2; one-story-per-repo tracking) via the Feb-11 arc; **Sept-22 the reverse-Omni spec method settled** (Omni-first over Flex POS, raw-transcript-in-git, rubber-duck 5-W interviews of Sasha, one-time exercise, working-group product-owner); Sept-24 reverse-Omni interviews entered execution (Kharetski self-driving w/ AI, Tumanov→data-center, Metelski/Makarych); **Sept-26 the "Jira Issue Type Workflows" written implementation guide** folded in (state machines for Value Stream/Initiative/Product/Feature; ChatGPT+Atlassian-MCP via Andrei Bosik; IP 90/747/726/327 hierarchy + rename IP 327→"Reich Rises"; both Omni & Reich Studio)** (25 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2025-04-07-recarve-gaming-platform-into-six-product-repos.md]] — keep the "Gaming Platform" (IP481) Jira initiative but re-carve into six product-repos (OmniCore, OmniLandBaseFramework, OmniOnlineFramework, LGS, RGS, OmniMath), each its own repository; residual code → main, new work via feature branches; Bosik mirrors the repos; submodule-vs-monorepo + sprint-length deferred; Apr-8 Jira-Plans naming execution (Omni-prefix, HHR→Land-Based-Overlay, Miranda→OmniCore, Vivien own repo) + GitHub-org-vs-value-stream open; aka six products, product per repository (3 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-24-single-prose-writing-standard.md]] — author ONE prose-writing standard from the best of the three-to-five existing variants and place it in the standards repository (owners Vladimir Samusenko and Evgeny Kharetski, Dima Chudinov consulted, due within a couple of days, Val monitoring), then run Claude over existing prose to normalize it; Val declined to write it himself; adjacent restatements: no code committed without matching prose (enforced as "commit yes, PR no"), prose in `docs/prose`, capabilities and requirements in parallel, bugs recorded not fixed; aka prose standard, prose document structure (2 sources, updated 2026-08-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-26-pavel-irina-own-nova-capabilities-to-jira-through-september.md]] — (Aug-26 2026, active) Pavel Frolov and Irina Shishko own the NOVA capabilities → MVP → Jira process through September; developers start on NOVA ~Oct 1; aka capabilities to MVP to Jira ownership, Oct 1 NOVA dev start (3 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-26-self-test-on-lw-sas-bench-in-georgia-plus-minsk-emulation.md]] — (Aug-26 2026, active) set up the Light & Wonder SAS test bench in the Georgia office and build a Minsk emulation of it (SAS emulation on VMs), so the team can self-test; aka L&W SAS test bench, SAS test bench Georgia (2 sources, updated 2026-08-26)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-28-reverse-engineer-acceptance-criteria-and-automate-qa-dragon-pays.md]] — (Aug-28 2026, active) reverse-engineer requirements and acceptance criteria from the ported Dragon Pays game and try to automate its QA, timeboxed one week (two max) with a review Fri Sept-4 2026; Igor Metelski runs it role-playing as QA on someone else's port; a second game ported to NOVA in parallel by Anton Leshkevich (line game, not Calle Ocho); anything that becomes a standard goes into the standards repository; migration itself proceeds as settled; aka Dragon Pays QA experiment, automate QA Rage to Nova (6 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-01-freeze-existing-manual-test-cases.md]] — (Sept-1 2026, active) freeze the existing hand-written test cases in their current warehouse ("я их как бы заморозил бы") rather than migrating or deleting them; Claude-written tests go into a new warehouse; aka freeze manual test cases (2 sources, updated 2026-09-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-03-prose-standard-into-knowledge-repository.md]] — (Sept-3 2026, active) the prose standard gets **exactly one location** — moved out of the LGS repo into the `knowledge` repository's standards folder — and the prose *skills* move into the Claude Code configuration; follows through on decisions/2026-08-24-single-prose-writing-standard, whose authoring was done but whose placement had failed; aka one home for the prose standard (5 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-03-module-contracts-and-nova-integration-repository.md]] — (Sept-3 2026, active) every NOVA module gets a **contract written by Claude, not by hand**, and a machine-side **NOVA integration repository** is created and populated (NOVA has none today; Flex-IQ does) — two milestones over roughly two weeks; aka module contracts, docs/contracts (4 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-04-data-contracts-closed-every-repository-by-september-11.md]] — (Sept-4 2026, active) Val closes the data-contract debate: every repository carries its own data contract by **Sept 11**, with 80% done judged acceptable ("80% сделано хорошо, если 100 лучше"), on a zero-trust input-contract model; the maths server is opened up alongside it — "у нас нету почти тайны в математике"; aka contracts by September 11, zero trust input contract (6 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-04-point-claude-at-the-standards-repository-first.md]] — (Sept-4 2026, active) standing instruction, given twice in one day: point the coding assistant at the **Knowledge Base / Standards folder in GitHub** before it writes anything; company-wide access was granted and **manually verified across all 39 accounts** — which also discharges the Sept-3 access commitment; aka point your code at the standards, 39 accesses (12 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-04-browser-pixi-stack-concern-closed.md]] — (Sept-4 2026, **superseded Oct 21 2026** — NOVA drops the browser for a native engine) Anton Leshkevich's objection to the browser/Pixi engine stack is raised, argued out against Unity, Unreal, Godot and OGRE, and **closed in favour of building the pipeline** rather than re-opening the engine question; aka tech stack concern closed, Godot experiment (4 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-04-asset-naming-convention-must-be-written-down.md]] — (Sept-4 2026, active) the mismatched-assets root cause named — "it was verbal agreement" — so the asset naming convention and unique game code names must be written down; the branch-selection rule was left **unresolved** in the same meeting; aka naming convention root cause, verbal agreement (2 sources, updated 2026-09-04)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-03-capabilities-consolidated-by-administrative-direction.md]] — (Sept-3 2026, active) fix over-granular capabilities by giving Claude an **administrative** direction, not an architectural one — roughly twenty capabilities per product, ~8 requirements and ~8 features each; the LGS set had come out at 54 capabilities, the Recycler at 34; aka capability granularity (2 sources, updated 2026-09-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-03-acceptance-criteria-settled-by-experiment.md]] — (Sept-3 2026, active) Val concedes the acceptance-criteria disagreement to an **experiment** (coin-in and a counter) rather than settling it by argument, and **Alexey Khamin — one person, not two** — owns attaching requirements to capabilities and auditing the acceptance criteria; aka AC audit ownership (2 sources, updated 2026-09-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-main-branch-must-always-build-and-the-code-belongs-to-the-project.md]] — Val's code-standards email read aloud in the room and confirmed **already in force**: main must always contain correct working code that anyone can pull and build into a working installer from **today's** release notes, and a failure means the code, the release note **or the prose** is wrong — with fixing it taking priority, which promotes prose/release-notes from documentation to a **build-health dependency**; **the code belongs to the project, not to the developer who wrote it**, so a tester/QA may propose and make a fix and raise a pull request for a reviewer to merge (Val grounds the permission in Claude Code — "особенно сегодня с использованием клад коуд… не камит, а сделать пулурек"); small frequent commits (2–3–4 a day, integration tests each time, ~300-line chunks) so review lands on a sane unit; Bosik's amendment accepted — someone-else-merges is a **preference, not an absolute** ("Всегда ктото должен, но мы всегда или часто находим исключение"); open — who merges when there is no second person, and which "points 1 and 4" Val meant (the transcript's plain reading and the notes' gloss differ, neither asserted); status active (3 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-flex-port-sas-mode-is-a-selection-capability-not-a-long-lived-branch.md]] — the branch argument and its resolution: Pavel Frolov objected from his long-lived Flex-Port SAS/AFT branch, Val conceded a branch may promise less than main until it merges, **Alexei Khamin corrected both** ("Да, есть возможность собрать из ветки и проверить"), Val refused the tag-vs-branch detour, and ruled that the **SAS / no-SAS split is a capability whose filter lives inside main**, not a branch; notable for Val naming the missing selection screen as **his own** specification gap ("тогда вал недосказал, что должен быть сортировочный экран"); carries the reversal Pavel reported — Val's **Sept-13** instruction that Flex-Port must also work on machines **without** SAS, "это как бы немножко ломает то, что я уже сделал", which is added as a fourth dated data point to the standing single-SAS open contradiction and **deliberately not resolved**; open — build-time vs device-parameter mode selection, and the real capability counts (Pavel "30" → "по порту будет меньше. Ну 10", deadline "к 1 октября"); status active (4 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-alekseev-is-walked-through-the-standards-by-bosik-not-ordered.md]] — how JVL brings a non-conforming engineer onto its standards: **Andrey Bosik books a meeting for the morning of Sept 15** inside Evgeniy Alekseev's 07:00–08:00 window and walks him through the standards **explaining reason, dependency and sequence rather than ordering** — the session where Val states the principle "explain the reason, don't say 'because we told you'"; Alekseev's working method recorded as engineering fact (local machine, very large single code drops, works alone, no branched-off branches, "tell me and I'll implement it") along with his 07:00–08:00 availability and that he leaves for his own job, plus the resourcing contingency if the standards are not adopted; **§15.8 — Val's repeated personal and performance assessments of two named engineers were deliberately NOT recorded**, only the working-method, coaching and resourcing facts, with exclusion notes on the page; open — whether the coaching meeting actually happened; status active (2 sources, updated 2026-09-19)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-nothing-in-mvp1-may-still-be-proposed-and-bosik-writes-the-exception-report.md]] — Val's Jira state chain made explicit: **nothing in MVP 1 may still sit in Proposed**, To Do carries features, features In Progress carry a linked branch, and capabilities link to requirements with acceptance criteria — with **Andrey Bosik** (DevOps, resolved by Val speaking the surname: "Андрей Босик, вы можете написать… эксепшн репорт?") to write the **exception report** that surfaces anything breaking the chain, to Val/Pavel/Klimovich; Klimovich's own job is framed as selling capabilities out of Proposed to the developers ("ваша задача пропуст в кавычках продать"); status active (6 sources, updated 2026-09-20)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-nobody-downloads-and-installs-builds-thirty-day-target.md]] — Val kills manual build download-and-install outright and puts a **30-day target** on the automatic update environment ("давайте себе поставим задачу сделать в течение 30 дней, хорошо?"), with **Flex-Port named as the remaining gap** — Pavel: "пока что мы не умеем обновлять флекспорт"; Bosik and Pavel jointly own finishing it; status active (2 sources, updated 2026-09-19)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-15-the-week-goes-to-non-functional-requirements-and-monday-september-21-is-the-deadline.md]] — **"Если это не написано, этого нету"** — Val repoints Wednesday to Friday at the **non-functional requirements** and names five owners verbatim ("дима чудинов, Андрей босик, Ирина шишко, Александр биратко и Павел Фролов"), with **Monday Sept 21 as the MVP1 grooming gate** ("в понедельник, 21 числа это последний день"); the same NFR work was already ruled first-priority on **Sept 7 and is still unwritten eight days later**, which is recorded as a dated escalation on that page rather than as a fresh decision; Chudinov's answer that some of it exists but undocumented ("требования не прописанные, но у нас реализована система графана") is the exact gap the rule targets; status active (8 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-15-capability-requires-requirement-and-dates-sit-on-the-lowest-level.md]] — the Jira link direction is **reversed to "capability REQUIRES requirement"** on Irina Shishko's correction, and **planning dates always sit on the lowest level of work** so the roll-up never breaks; status active (2 sources, updated 2026-09-19)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-23-capability-118-is-split-by-product-and-two-devices-keep-two-repositories.md]] — Sept-23 2026: Pavel splits CAP-118 so FlexPay has its own capability; the two devices keep two repositories for now (3 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-24-written-records-go-by-email-and-chats-are-for-instant-matters.md]] — Val (Sept-24 2026): written records go by email, chats are for instant matters; Klimovich emails a Jira change log at the end of any day he changes Jira (6 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-24-capabilities-sit-in-one-flat-list-under-each-platform-and-releases-are-timeline-lines-not-initiatives.md]] — Val (Sept-24 2026): under each platform capabilities sit in one flat list (views from filters); releases are Jira timeline lines, not release-named initiatives; top stream Core (old IP 738 → Tools); product IPs removed; value streams Games/Core/Hardware; Galaxy structure still open (3 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-25-one-company-second-brain-feeds-an-ai-project-manager-for-jira.md]] — Val (Sept-25 2026): one company second brain (Karpathy method) feeds an AI project manager pointed at the GitHub repos — "only 20 people" limit, ESL English; design homework due Tue Sept 29 7:00 (3 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-28-a-capability-is-one-high-level-line-and-the-product-owner-does-not-tell-engineers-how.md]] — Val (Sept-28 2026): a capability is one high-level line ("Replace battery without factory reset"); the product owner states what he wants, engineers write how (3 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-29-the-fix-goes-out-as-a-re-release-not-a-hack-and-only-that-commit-goes-in.md]] — Val's ruling (as Pavel relayed it): the modem fix is re-released as fast as possible, not slipped onto a production machine; Irina's one-commit rule; build 4.50.2; library change declared as "connectivity"; aka перевыпускать, no hack, 4502 (5 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-29-the-amd-environment-is-rebuilt-from-the-rk3568-sdk-pavels-ten-day-spike-and-the-rk3576-waits.md]] — The AMD development environment is rebuilt from the RK3568 SDK as a skeleton: Pavel takes the spike himself, MVP 1 = kernel, root file system, installer and bootloader, ten days with a review on the 8th; the RK3576 waits until the two environments are standardised; RK and AMD stay separate repositories; aka AMD SDK spike, x86 SDK from the RK3568 skeleton, standardise first (8 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-30-an-autotest-task-that-cannot-finish-goes-to-blocked-not-closed.md]] — Pavel's rule for Vladimir's task 41: an autotest task stopped by defects goes to Blocked (defects linked), not closed, is raised at the next meeting; next task = the one closest to ready, dates moved; Irina: any unassigned task can be taken; aka в блок положить, task 41 Blocked, более в готовом состоянии (4 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-01-completed-is-the-developers-last-step-and-a-found-problem-sends-the-feature-from-completed-back-to-to-do-as-a-story.md]] — Oct 1 2026: "Completed" is the developer's last step on a feature; a problem found while development is still going is a Story, not a Bug, and sends the feature Completed → To Do (Kovalchuk adds the transition); features link to the requirements they cover; Request Review was Lena's team's status (Pavel, Irina); aka из комплект в туду, story not bug (7 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-05-a-capability-moves-itself-to-request-review-when-all-its-features-are-completed-and-a-new-story-sends-feature-and-capability-back-to-to-do.md]] — all child features Completed → the capability goes to Request Review automatically (Kovalchuk's weekend automations); a story under a Completed feature sends the feature to To Do and the capability from Request Review to To Do, automated, developer moves to In Progress; stories must hang under a parent (Irina, Chudinov, Kovalchuk, Oct 5 2026); aka Jira reopen rules, 4 автоматизации, фичу из комплитов в туду (8 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-05-a-release-bakes-a-file-of-the-component-versions-it-contains-into-the-artifact.md]] — every release carries a file listing the component versions it contains inside its artifact; the integration-repository manifest need not pin release versions (artists and autotests need snapshots); Kharetski plans a GitHub Page with a "release" tick (Kharetski + Pavel, Oct 5 2026); aka релиз должен запекать какие версии, GitHub Page release tick (4 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-30-engineers-never-change-msbc-and-administration-never-changes-github.md]] — Val's border rule: supplier/financial data only in MSBC, engineering files only in GitHub, neither side edits the other; crossed only by a "transcriber" tool carrying flat revisions one way; aka non-penetrable border, engineering territory and administrative territory (3 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-30-a-new-part-number-is-assigned-by-claude-from-the-standard-in-github-and-pushed-to-msbc-once.md]] — Claude assigns new part numbers from the written standard in the GitHub "standards" repo, pushed to MSBC once at creation (Genadi: "Perfect"); Lev's caveat that a BC item also needs posting groups, dimensions, units of measure; evolves Aug-12 "BC assigns numbers"; aka part number from the standard, two sources of input (2 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-01-only-the-finished-bom-goes-into-msbc-the-configurator-is-ai-logic-outside-it-no-hybrid-and-the-pilot-is-the-flex-pay-slim.md]] — Val: only the finished BOM goes into MSBC; the "configurator" that builds it from the flat GitHub list is AI logic outside MSBC; no hybrid; prices stay out of GitHub; pilot = Claude Code pulls the Flex Pay Slim part number flat with all suppliers, then a two-hour session with Genadi, whose doubt is unchanged; aka AI configurator, конфигуратор, no hybrid, Flex Pay Slim pilot (4 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-29-bosik-owns-the-ai-pm-the-meeting-bot-waits-and-the-second-brain-is-built-first.md]] — Bosik owns the AI PM; live meeting bot to MVP 2; collect transcripts and build the second brain first; drafts to repository code owners, no human "responsible"; dry run before Jira writes; status Fri Oct 2 ~7:00; aka AI draft status, никаких бонусов — held Oct 2: 318 transcripts collected, next status Tuesday Oct 6 at 7 (7 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-02-ai-pm-mvp1-uses-the-teams-transcripts-as-they-are-and-whisper-re-transcription-waits-for-mvp2.md]] — AI PM MVP 1 works from Microsoft's Teams transcripts as they are; Whisper-with-glossary re-transcription goes to MVP 2 (volume, time, cost); the 318 transcripts are stored in GitHub, a database maybe later (Bosik, Val not objecting); aka Whisper to MVP 2, перевёл всё в MVP 2 (2 sources, updated 2026-10-05)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-05-conversion-tools-and-tests-leave-the-local-computer-now-and-claude-proposes-the-repository-layout.md]] — no conversion files kept locally; tools go into Igor's current repo for now; tests come only from acceptance criteria; Claude to propose the repo layout (Oct 5 2026); aka спайк, next review Thursday 7:00 (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-05-nathan-carver-runs-the-flex-pay-slim-bom-reverse-spike-and-flex-port-follows.md]] — Nathan flattens the MSBC Flex Pay Slim BOM into GitHub, rebuilds it through repos, data contracts and agents, pushes it back and compares; Flex Port next; Jira DTP-1083 (Oct 5 2026); aka BOM reverse spike (7 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-05-hardware-follows-the-developer-repo-model-one-jira-project-one-repo-zero-trust-data-contracts-no-monorepo.md]] — hardware follows the developer repo model: one Jira project = one repo, zero trust, prose + ADRs + a data contract per repo; GitHub holds a flat list and the BOM is generated like a build (Oct 5 2026); the "one Jira project = one repo, no monorepo" element reversed Oct 21 — one hardware repository with subfolders; aka zero trust repos for hardware, ISO image analogy (12 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-06-built-capabilities-without-requirements-get-a-review-session-and-the-developer-adds-missing-texts-for-andrei-to-approve.md]] — built work with no requirements gets a review session; the developer adds missing screen texts and opens a ticket for "Andrei" to approve (Oct 6 2026); aka test 69 (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-07-cover-the-code-with-tests-first-and-the-ci-hardware-runs-and-product-repository-hookup-wait.md]] — write tests first; the CI hardware runs and the product-repository hookup wait (Oct 7 2026, Pavel with Irina); aka test coverage first, покрытие тестами в первую очередь (3 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-08-the-ai-pm-goes-live-in-real-jira-projects-on-october-12-on-its-current-architecture-without-lenas-meetings.md]] — the AI PM goes live in real Jira projects on Oct 12 on its current architecture; Lena's meetings leave the pilot; the agent deletes only its own items and comments on others (Oct 8 2026); aka боевой режим, AI Draft lifetime (19 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-08-an-ai-chief-system-architect-maps-galaxy-and-nova-from-code-prose-and-data-contracts-to-find-gaps-as-bosiks-next-objective.md]] — an AI Chief System Architect maps Galaxy and NOVA from code, prose and data contracts (HTML block diagrams, harness links) to find gaps — Bosik's next objective (Oct 8 2026); aka AI chief architect persona (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-08-msbc-stops-being-the-bom-source-and-the-week-of-october-12-goes-to-ordering-without-mikhail.md]] — MSBC stops being the BOM source and keeps only vendor financial/admin data; the week of Oct 12 goes to Nathan's BOM work so JVL can order without Mikhail; the Texas BOM goes into BC now (Oct 8 2026); aka ordering without Misha, Texas BOM in BC (7 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-09-tests-to-october-15-follow-80-20-and-port-machine-and-iq-tests-come-before-cloud-tests.md]] — tests to Oct 15 follow 80/20: main functions first, port/machine/IQ tests before cloud tests (Oct 9 2026); aka принцип 80 20 (3 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-09-the-old-usb-updater-repository-is-archived-because-rauc-now-does-usb-updates.md]] — the old USB updater repository is archived because RAUC now does USB updates; full reinstall is by micro-SD (Oct 9 2026); aka апдейтер, RAUC (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-09-the-georgia-flex-pay-slim-bom-is-built-forward-from-genadis-github-source-by-agent-and-script-with-human-approval-by-end-of-october.md]] — the Georgia Flex Pay Slim BOM is built forward from Genadi's GitHub flat list by agent and script, approved by a human, then pushed to MSBC — by end of October (Oct 9 2026); aka Pay Slim first real test, trust and verify (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-12-flexport-ci-tests-run-on-real-ports-through-the-internal-runner-and-no-port-emulator-is-built-for-now.md]] — Flexport CI tests run on real ports through the internal self-hosted runner; no STM32 port emulator for now (Oct 12 2026); aka no port emulator, self-hosted runner (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-12-separate-flex-iq-version-numbers-per-environment-are-not-an-mvp1-blocker-and-a-fix-comes-after-mvp1.md]] — separate Flex IQ version counters per environment are not an MVP 1 blocker; a shared scheme comes after MVP 1 (Oct 12 2026); aka production starts from one (2 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-13-the-agent-builds-the-bom-as-a-control-gate-taught-by-data-contracts-not-cad-and-genadi-finds-why-it-is-wrong.md]] — the agent-built BOM is the control gate for whether AI understands the product; Genadi finds why it is wrong rather than fixing it; taught by data contracts, not CAD (Oct 13 2026); aka BOM control gate, 70 percent right (5 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-13-procurement-reports-come-only-from-msbc-and-the-excel-export-report-goes-away.md]] — procurement reports come only from MSBC; the Excel export report goes away; a consultant builds the reports and Nathan links them into MCP (Oct 13 2026); aka Misha's Excel report (4 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-14-the-ai-pm-keeps-its-0-80-confidence-threshold-and-meetings-get-more-concrete-instead.md]] — Val (Oct 14 2026): do not lower the AI PM's 0.80 confidence threshold for now; people in meetings must discuss tasks more concretely and instruct the PM clearly (≥0.80 creates a task or records a decision; below it nothing is done); aka keep the 0.80 threshold, порог 0,80, не понижать порог (6 sources, updated 2026-10-17)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-18-no-private-calls-with-the-ai-pm-it-should-speak-at-the-meeting-itself.md]] — Val (Oct 18): no private calls with the AI PM; it speaks at the meeting (summary, questions to each person, untasked topics of the last 2 weeks); voice due about Nov 8; aka give the PM the floor (2 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-18-evgeny-kharetski-owns-a-voice-ai-game-design-assistant-with-a-first-pass-reviewed-oct-25.md]] — Val (Oct 18): a voice AI Game Design Assistant questions the head of game design and outputs a creative direction document to Igor's spec; Evgeny Kharetski owns it, Igor checks; new Jira project and repo; first pass reviewed Sun Oct 25; aka Game Design Assistant (4 sources, updated 2026-10-24)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-10-21-pavel-frolov-is-product-owner-of-the-georgia-commissioning-chatbot-and-andrey-bosik-develops-it.md]] — Val (Oct 21): Pavel is product owner and Andrey Bosik developer of a chatbot that answers Intralot's commissioning call placed from the machine; calls recorded, failures go to a live technician; aka commissioning chatbot (4 sources, updated 2026-10-24)

### Games & Design
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-01-28-gli-omni-certification-runs-on-jvl-white-papers.md]] — Val (Jan-28 2026): GLI certification of Omni runs on JVL-written white papers that GLI reviews; GLI's proposal waits until it has read them; one channel via Val and Juan (3 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-03-no-en-masse-rage-to-nova-migration.md]] — (Aug-3 2026, active) do NOT migrate RAGE games to NOVA en masse; port the common NOVA environment + build new games on it, convert old games only on-demand per market; fully port the South Dakota product to NOVA (~10→12 games) over ~6 months (3 transition + 3 polishing); don't finish/certify standalone Calle Ocho; next experiment = horizontal SD game (Nikena) with logic, reviewed Aug 17 (3 sources, updated 2026-09-20)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-08-14-first-nova-product-south-dakota-vertical.md]] — (Aug-14 2026, active but titular claim SUPERSEDED) release sequencing V1000/Rage → FP7/NOVA: ~~South Dakota Vertical 01 = first NOVA product (~March 2027)~~ — **owner ruled 2026-09-01 that the first NOVA product is South Dakota VLT-2** (see [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-01-first-nova-product-south-dakota-vlt-2.md]]); the rest stands; Nebraska D2702 stays on Rage (end-2026); Georgia V3 stays current-platform (Sept-1), NOVA a later "V4-like" GA release; submit Calle Ocho (already on NOVA) to GLI to certify the platform; Lena builds NOVA games in parallel; Peach bonus dead / games onto Liquid Glass; SD Vertical needs 3 new games (Solar Keno, Aaron's Pub, Dakota Bison) built not converted; refines decisions/2026-08-03-no-en-masse (3 sources, updated 2026-08-21)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-08-bofa-scope-prior-day-reporting-ach-debits-by-file.md]] — (Sept-8 2026, active) scope the Bank of America integration as **prior-day reporting only** (no current-day need), with ACH debits forced onto a NACHA file because BofA has no ACH-debit API — a hybrid of API reporting and file-based payments, with no sandbox available before CashPro is in place; aka BofA scope, reporting by API payments by file (4 sources, updated 2026-10-14)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-08-credits-not-currency-on-the-buttons-and-two-games-remathed.md]] — (Sept-8 2026, active — taken 9:00 PM that evening, reported the next morning) put **credits, not currency, on the buttons**, and re-math two games to suit; Efim Podvoiski estimated ~14 hours, due Sept 11; aka credits not currency (2 sources, updated 2026-09-09)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-georgia-class-a-v43-is-built-on-nova-not-rage.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) the Georgia Class A V43 is built on **NOVA, not RAGE** — "it's really a bad idea to do it on Rage… Rage has served so well to us. Let's just now park it. Kiss it, say our goodbyes, and move on." Michael Gottlieb objected and withdrew; Efim Podvoiski's counter was decisive. A Jan-1 goal moved to **Feb-1**, Nebraska takes precedence, ~101 days quoted, Line Switches as the test bed. **No RAGE sunset DATE is set — the sunset is an event, not a calendar entry — and "GLI" appears nowhere in the source, so NOVA → GLI remains unscheduled and the Feb-1 figure is a product date, not a certification date.** Carries two open contradictions; aka Class A on Nova, "let's just now park it" (5 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-no-new-game-badge-and-two-titles-per-category-stand.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) two home-screen rulings **Val lost** — no "new game" badge (players "care if it has progressives"), and two titles per category stands — alongside his explicit statement of where his authority stops: "I don't direct the design"; aka paradox of choice (4 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-ip-887-renamed-v43-and-kept-in-backlog-not-retired.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) Val proposed retiring IP-887 and was **overruled**: rename it V43 and keep it in the backlog. The cause was a "two South Dakotas" confusion — one the NOVA D27, the other the RAGE V43; aka two South Dakotas, "I live and die by Jira" (2 sources, updated 2026-09-11)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-no-changes-in-rage-studio-everything-lands-on-omni.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) no further changes go into RAGE Studio — every fix lands on OMNI, and RAGE back-ports are chosen only once the capabilities exist; the field complaints driving it are the unhelpful "device not found" / "IO board not found" errors; aka no changes in RAGE Studio (2 sources, updated 2026-09-11)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-the-passport-is-preserved-and-jvl-is-using-the-bindings-wrongly-in-this-market.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) the Passport peripheral-binding mechanism is **kept** — "паспорт убивать не надо" — but JVL is using it wrongly for this market: record and flag component changes rather than forbid them, and let the operator nominate who may update it. A **third** internal position on the passport, added as a new open question rather than resolving the Sept-2 vs Sept-10 split; aka do not confuse RIS and passport (4 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-new-regulations-for-the-passport-and-ris-talked-out-monday-and-converted-from-the-transcript.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) the new Passport/RIS regulations get talked out in a Monday Sept-14 9:30 session, then converted **from the transcript** into capabilities via Andrey Bosik — ~75% in one pass, with a second session to reach ~90%; aka "70 percent in an hour" (2 sources, updated 2026-09-11)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-market-access-traded-for-a-share-of-the-back-end-and-the-atm-fee-belongs-to-the-master-operator.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) Val will not carry anyone's card without a share of the back-end profit — "this is where the money is at… my goal is to derive my profit from managing cash" — and the ATM fee belongs to the master operator. Opens a **new open contradiction**: Val said on Sept-2 that "InComm gives me 0.5 percent of the processing fee" and on Sept-11 that "InComm doesn't offer any profit sharing on the other side", nine days apart; aka a share of the back end (2 sources, updated 2026-09-11)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-mvp1-goes-with-flex-iq-alone-and-one-kiosk-per-location.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) October 1 goes with **one configuration only — Flex IQ**; FlexPay moves to MVP 2 and the Flex-Port stays; aka "we finally decide we go with only one configuration" (4 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-mvp1-boundary-bill-escrow-and-pin-out-remote-update-and-master-device-in.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) the MVP 1 boundary drawn: **out** — bill escrow, player PIN, remote config; **in** — remote update, Flex-IQ software/firmware management, the Flex-Port master device, with one Amazon S3 store for all firmware; aka Flex IQ is PIN-free (2 sources, updated 2026-09-11)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-one-card-at-a-thousand-dollars-and-the-rest-stays-on-the-ticket.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) a payout over the card limit issues **one $1,000 card** and the remainder stays on the ticket or e-wallet; split logic rejected and parked on MVP 2. Note one speaker renders the limit as $2,000 in the same session — flagged on the page as a likely slip, **not reconciled**; aka the rest stays on the ticket (4 sources, updated 2026-09-19)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-lease-blocking-reaches-the-flex-ports-and-is-never-automatic.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active, narrowed Oct-18 by owner ruling) lease blocking reaches the Flex-Ports so players cannot play; blocking a sold Flex machine for non-payment stays **manual** ("автоматически мы никогда не блокируем"), while the payment-processing flow follows the Oct-14 automatic location block (MVP 1.5); aka never block automatically (9 sources, updated 2026-10-17)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-11-mudagoose-never-in-mvp1-and-its-code-comes-out-at-mvp3.md]] — (Sept-11 2026, active) MudaGoose is **never** in MVP 1 — confirmed on Val's explicit "я бы хотел бы для транскрипта, чтоб вы подтвердили" — and its code removal is assigned to MVP 3 at ~20% of the time; aka MudaGoose out (2 sources, updated 2026-09-11)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-ewallet-ttl-defaults-to-thirty-days-and-is-set-per-location.md]] — an e-wallet gets a **time-to-live: 30 days by default, configurable per location from 1 to 365** ("По дефолту есть предложение установить 30 дней, но это конфигурируем параметр для каждой отдельной локации"), with the validity period **printed on the carrier** and already-printed tickets never reprinted; empty wallets are deliberately kept rather than cleaned up because separate logic would cost more (Pavel: "Нам проще его держать, чем придумывать отдельную логику работы с пустыми тикетами"); **this closes the April-2025 open question** of whether wallet validity is 30 days or ~24 hours, marked resolved in place; open — what happens to an existing wallet when a location changes its TTL; status active (6 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-the-ewallet-is-created-before-its-ticket-prints.md]] — the wallet is created at the moment the "print new" button is pressed, **before** printing, so a dead printer cannot lose the player's money; the cashier recovers it from the transaction list; the Flex-Port collect timeout is **currently about 30 seconds**, after which "все потом эти деньги исчезают", and the task of changing that has passed from Pavel Frolov (who tried and failed) to **Evgeny Kharetski** — his first transactional/Flex-Port task in the corpus; **reissue-vs-reprint is parked, not decided**, and "what the cashier does with an unclaimed wallet" stays open; status active (6 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-mvp1-stays-local-and-the-cloud-balance-requirement-moves-to-mvp2.md]] — **MVP 1 keeps wallet balances on the terminal**; requirement **1538** is lifted off capability **158** into a new MVP 2 cloud capability, and the MVP 1 dashboard shows activated cards only; the trigger is a tooling symptom worth recording — Dzmitry Chudzinau reports Claude going in circles trying to close a capability whose requirement demands a cloud balance ("клод начинает с ума сходить… у нас тут баланс должен быть в облаке. Я начинаю создавать эти фичи"), i.e. an unbuildable requirement surfacing as AI thrash rather than as a design review; status active (10 sources, updated 2026-10-17)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-capabilities-are-written-against-the-published-sas-standard.md]] — capabilities are written against the **published Gaming Standards Association SAS standard**, and Val targets **6.02 rather than the newest 6.03** because field machines lag ("на некоторых машинах они не сделали апдейт ещё на 602… давайте 602 хотя бы"), with Pavel confirming 6.03 is current; Klimovich to learn SAS 6.02 AFT, Biratka to supply the spec, Val to get it from the GSA if needed; open — whether the 6.02-vs-6.03 gap matters for AFT; the organisation Val named for the introduction is garbled ("чиллаи") and **left unresolved, not guessed**; status active (2 sources, updated 2026-09-19)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-14-one-report-must-make-mvp1-cards-issued-for-a-georgia-lottery-inspection.md]] — exactly **one** report has to ship in MVP 1 and the reason is regulatory, not analytical: when a Georgia Lottery inspection arrives at a location and asks to see the cards issued over a period, staff must produce it by pressing **one button** ("нажать одну кнопку"), reproduced from a report a competitor already provides ("у меня есть пример такого отчёта, который делает один из наших конкурентов"); open — what exactly goes on it and whether it fits the printer; status active (2 sources, updated 2026-09-19)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-15-balance-is-total-playable-only-and-redeemable-everywhere.md]] — a wallet balance is **three lines everywhere — Total / Playable only / Redeemable**, where playable-only + redeemable = total, with **no separate engineering vocabulary** behind the UI words; Biratka sourced "playable only" to the SAS spec itself ("такая же терминология присутствует и в сас спецификации"), Chudinov gave the two-balance reason and the spend priority (playable money first, then redeemable), and **Val declared it an ADR for the repo** ("Это является ad r… мы в repo должны иметь всегда эй диарс"); promo money parked to MVP 2/3; open and unresolved — whether there are two counters or three (Chudinov "формально баланса 2" against Irina "3 будет счётчика"); status active (5 sources, updated 2026-09-20)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-15-a-timeout-sends-the-money-to-unclaimed-and-the-player-never-loses-it.md]] — **"игрок никогда не может потерять свои деньги невозможно нельзя"** — a collect timeout must never destroy money, so the mechanism is an *unclaimed-money* wallet created, funded and never printed (Biratka's proposal); the spec must come from **AFT plus state banking law via Juan Martinez, then GLI**, and the whole thing is **explicitly not MVP 1**; open — where the unclaimed entity lives, who owns the balance, and whether it is one wallet or many; status active (8 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-15-the-flex-port-idle-screen-never-sleeps-and-the-port-mirrors-the-machine.md]] — the Flex-Port idle screen **loses its buttons and never sleeps**, the scanner runs permanently (Chudinov: "Вот уже год стоят наши включены, не отключаются и работают"), language becomes a top-right on-the-fly toggle, and **maintenance and lockout are two distinct signals**; the port **mirrors the machine even when the Georgia Lottery is the one issuing the block** — Val's "они пользуются первым саспортом, блокируют машины", followed by his concession to the room, "Вы вы более гуманитарные люди, чем я"; open — can the scanner be switched off, and Spanish by Oct 1; status active (4 sources, updated 2026-09-20)
- [[wiki/decisions/2026-09-15-the-flex-iq-cashier-flow-login-redemption-receipts-and-records.md]] — the Flex IQ cashier flow settled end to end: **4-digit PIN with Cancel removed**, plus Val's requirement that PIN **or** magstripe be selectable (the magstripe reader stays in the hardware, confirmed with Genadi Peari); redemption **pre-fills the maximum redeemable** and freezes on continue; the **activation receipt always prints while top-up receipts are optional** (narrowing the Sept-2 mandatory-receipt ruling rather than reversing it); records get date and direction filters; status active (5 sources, updated 2026-09-28)
